issues.description: The textual instructions require the Farm to use a Set (HashSet) to store unique animals and to initialize the HashSet in the no-arg constructor, but the provided solution implements the Farm using a List (ArrayList). This mismatch between the problem specification and the solution implementation can confuse students about which collection type to use and which semantics (uniqueness) are expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution (and template hint) consistent with the problem text by using a Set<Animal> and initializing it with a new HashSet<>() in the no-argument Farm constructor. Update addAnimal, getAnimals, and setAnimals to use Set<Animal> accordingly. Alternatively, if the intended design is a List, update the problem statement text to state List/ArrayList instead of Set/HashSet.

issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal inconsistency: the UML diagram shows Farm.animals typed as List<Animal>, but the textual Part 3 instructions explicitly require using a Set (HashSet) for unique animals. This contradiction can mislead students about the intended data structure.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: either (a) change the UML diagram to show animals: Set<Animal> (and mention HashSet in the UML notes) or (b) change the textual instructions to require a List/ArrayList. Prefer (a) if uniqueness is important to the learning objective.
